text.p: These are the leading storied in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey interested in importing meat and wheat from Yugoslavia, said Haka Oglay, first secretary of the Turkish embassy in Belgrade.

- November 3 elections showed citizens' increasing trust in socialists and their coalition partners both in Serbia and Montenegro. The total number of ballots of 1.84 million is significantly higher than in the prevous 1992 federal elections.

- John Shattuck, Assistant U.S State Secretary for Human Rights said Yugoslav cooperation with the Hague tribunal for war crimes and free media main were prerequisites for the country's complete return to the world organisations.
- John Kornblum, special U.S. envoy for Balkan, to arrive to Belgrade on Tuesday, to discuss Kosovo issue.
- Payment operations between Slovenia and Yugoslavia re-established.
- Montengrin President Momir Bulatovic announced that republic's police could arrest former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic if he came to visit his native Montenegro.
- U.N. administrator for Croatia's Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein to meet Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Friday and discuss extention of U.N. madate in the region.
- Nebojsa Medojevic, advisor in Montengrin Agency for foreign investments said federation was slowing down privatisation in this Yugoslav republic.
- Yugoslav constructors claim $650 million from abroad, said Branko Popovic of the Serbian constructors' trade union. -- Belgrade Newsroom, 381 11 222 4254
